```typescript
// internal/mcp-server/src/tools/simulate_cost.ts
import { simulateCost } from '@internal/cost-simulator'

export const inputSchema = {

  type: 'object',
  required: ['profile'],
  properties: {
    profile: {
      enum: ['p-solo', 'p-hobby', 'p-startup-small', 'p-startup-scale', 'p-enterprise'],
    },
    overrides: { type: 'object' },
  },
} as const

export const outputSchema = {
  $schema: 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema',
  type: 'object',
  required: [
    'profile',
    'monthly_total_usd',
    'by_layer',
    'by_provider',
    'assumptions',
    'prices_as_of',
  ],
  properties: {
    profile: {
      enum: ['p-solo', 'p-hobby', 'p-startup-small', 'p-startup-scale', 'p-enterprise'],
    },
    monthly_total_usd: { type: 'number', minimum: 0 },
    by_layer: {
      type: 'object',
      required: ['compute', 'storage', 'egress', 'registry', 'secrets', 'observability_saas'],
      properties: {
        compute: { type: 'number', minimum: 0 },
        storage: { type: 'number', minimum: 0 },
        egress: { type: 'number', minimum: 0 },
        registry: { type: 'number', minimum: 0 },
        secrets: { type: 'number', minimum: 0 },
        observability_saas: { type: 'number', minimum: 0 },
      },
    },
    by_provider: {
      type: 'object',
      additionalProperties: { type: 'number', minimum: 0 },
    },
    assumptions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    prices_as_of: { type: 'string', format: 'date' },
  },
} as const

export async function handler(input: {
  profile: 'p-solo' | 'p-hobby' | 'p-startup-small' | 'p-startup-scale' | 'p-enterprise'
  overrides?: Record<string, unknown>
}): Promise<unknown> {

}

export const meta = {
  name: 'simulate_cost',
  description: 'Estimate $/mo per layer from data/cloud-prices/* and the profile resource shape.',

} as const
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement root AGENTS.md**

  ```markdown
  <!-- AGENTS.md -->

  # AGENTS.md — Root

  Cascading agent guidance for `ts-monorepo-template`. Nearest-ancestor-wins
  lookup from any working directory; child overrides parent (spec Section 15.8).

  ## What this repo is

  A polyglot Nx monorepo template with seven architectural layers plus two
  entrypoint layers:

  - Layer 0a — Launcher CLI (`npx create-platform@latest`) and marketing site
  - Layer 0b — MCP server (`@ts-monorepo-template/mcp-server`)
  - Layer 1 — Verb surface (Taskfile)
  - Layer 2 — Toolchain (`devenv.nix`) + secrets (`secretspec`)
  - Layer 3 — Build orchestration (Nx + Nx Cloud)
  - Layer 4 — Container build (BuildKit + cosign)
  - Layer 5 — App runtime (Helm library chart)
  - Layer 6 — Platform infra (Crossplane XRDs + ESO)
  - Layer 7 — Bootstrap (Terraform + Ansible, optional)

  ## Founder-safe verbs (Layer 1)

  Engineers and agents type `task <verb>`. The full catalog lives in
  `Taskfile.yml`; the curated subset:

  - `task init` — run the launcher CLI wizard (alias of `npx create-platform`)
  - `task launch` — provision + deploy per the selected profile
  - `task open` — open Grafana, Argo CD, and the repo in the browser
  - `task profile:select` — re-run profile recommender + emit ADR
  - `task profile:fork` — derive a custom profile from a base
  - `task meta:validate` — validate every `META.yaml` against the v1 schema
  - `task adr:new` — scaffold a new ADR from `docs/adrs/_template.md`
  - `task adr:index` — regenerate `docs/adrs/README.md`
  - `task audit:append` / `audit:verify` / `audit:export` / `audit:diff`
  - `task docs:gen` — regenerate `apps/docs-public/` from code
  - `task ci:per-commit` — replay every CI gate across the local commit ladder

  ## Never-do list

  - Never write a plaintext `.env.local`. The only secret surface is
    `secretspec` (Layer 2). AKV is the source of truth; OS keyring is cache.
  - Never bypass git hooks (`--no-verify`). Fix the hook environment instead.
  - Never amend + force-push without explicit human authorization.
  - Never provision stateful infra from an app Helm chart. Stateful infra is
    Crossplane-only (Layer 6).
  - Never commit the Nx Cloud access token. It lives only in GH Actions secrets.
  - Never claim a directory's META.yaml without resolving the cascade upwards.

  ## How agents read this repo

  1. Resolve `AGENTS.md` upwards (this file → `apps/AGENTS.md` → ...).
  2. Resolve `META.yaml` upwards with the same rule.
  3. Use the MCP server tools (`list_profiles`, `describe_app`, `claim_infra`,
     `simulate_cost`, `explain_tradeoff`, `propose_change`) — they read the
     same META.yaml graph.

  See `docs/agents/agents-md-cascade.md` and `docs/agents/mcp-tool-reference.md`
  for the full agent surface.
  ```

  ```markdown
  <!-- apps/AGENTS.md -->

  # AGENTS.md — apps/

  ## App-build conventions

  - Every app has `META.yaml` (kind: App) + `README.md` + `AGENTS.md` (per-app
    override below). Cascade resolves child-wins from any subdirectory.
  - Build: `task build:<svc>`. Test: `task test:<svc>`. Lint: `task lint:<svc>`.
  - Each app ships a multi-stage `Dockerfile` per Layer 4 template. No app
    builds its own runtime image flags — use `internal/templates/dockerfiles/`.
  - Apps consume infra via `META.yaml` `spec.claims[]`. Never write raw
    connection strings; ESO injects via the Crossplane-published Secret.

  ## Per-app override

  Each `apps/<svc>/AGENTS.md` follows the spec Section 15.8 per-app template:
  What this app is / Build-test-lint / Architecture invariants / Common tasks /
  Out of scope / How to claim infra / How to add a new endpoint.
  ```

  ```markdown
  <!-- packages/AGENTS.md -->

  # AGENTS.md — packages/

  ## Library conventions

  - Libraries are TypeScript-first; polyglot SDKs ship as separate sibling
    libraries under `packages/<name>-{go,py,rs}/` when needed.
  - Public API surface lives in `packages/<lib>/src/index.ts`. No deep imports
    from consumers.
  - Never import from sibling apps. Libraries cannot depend on apps; apps
    depend on libraries.
  - Generated code from `packages/contracts/` (buf) is committed under
    `gen/{go,ts,py,rs}/` so non-TS apps can build without a TS toolchain.
  ```

  ```markdown
  <!-- internal/AGENTS.md -->

  # AGENTS.md — internal/

  ## Schemas, error catalog, glossary editing rules

  - JSON Schemas live under `internal/schemas/`. The discriminator on
    `META.yaml` is `kind`; valid values enumerated in
    `internal/schemas/meta-v1.schema.json`.
  - Adding a new `kind` requires updating the schema, the validator
    (`task meta:validate`), and the MCP `meta.validate` tool fixtures.
  - Plain-English errors live in `internal/errors/catalog.yaml`. Every entry
    has `code`, `founder`, `engineer`, `link`. The launcher renderer and MCP
    `errors.lookup` both read this file — do not duplicate.
  - Glossary terms live in `internal/glossary/terms.yaml`. Each term cross-
    references the spec section where it is load-bearing.
  - The CLI scaffold lives in `internal/cli/`; the MCP server in
    `internal/mcp-server/`; the recommender in `internal/recommender/`; the
    cost simulator in `internal/cost-simulator/`. None of these are shipped
    as runtime apps — they are tooling.
  ```

  ```markdown
  <!-- infra/AGENTS.md -->

  # AGENTS.md — infra/

  ## Conventions

  ### Helm

  - The only Helm artifact apps depend on is `infra/helm/lib-chart/`. Per-app
    charts under `infra/helm/apps/<svc>/` are exactly 3 files: `Chart.yaml`
    (deps lib-chart), `values.yaml` (defaults), `values.{env}.yaml` (overlays).
  - SecurityContext FLOOR + NetworkPolicy default-deny are enforced by the
    library chart. Apps cannot relax them; they can only narrow further.

  ### Crossplane

  - XRDs live under `infra/crossplane/xrds/<x>/`. Each XRD owns one resource
    family (XPostgres, XCache, XBlob, ...).
  - Compositions live under `infra/crossplane/compositions/`. Selection is
    profile-driven via `profiles/<id>/crossplane/composition-pins.yaml`.
  - Stateful infra is Crossplane-only. App Helm charts never provision DBs.

  ### Argo CD

  - Root app at `infra/argocd/root/`. ApplicationSet matrices fan out per env.
  - Promotion via Kargo Stages (Day-1: `go-hello`). Do not hand-promote.

  ### Terraform / Ansible (Layer 7)

  - Modules under `infra/terraform/modules/<provider>/` (Contabo, Hetzner,
    OVH, Azure, AWS, GCP, Cloudflare). Envs under `infra/terraform/envs/`.
  - Kubespray-style configurable Ansible playbooks under `infra/ansible/`.
  - Bootstrap is opt-in: default assumes a working kubeconfig.
  ```

  ```markdown
  # AGENTS.md — profiles/

  ## Profile authoring rules

  The 5 named profiles (spec Section 1.5):

  | Founder label       | Machine ID        | $/mo band |
  | ------------------- | ----------------- | --------- |
  | Just Me             | `p-solo`          | $0        |
  | Side Project        | `p-hobby`         | $5-20     |
  | Early Startup       | `p-startup-small` | $30-150   |
  | Scaling Startup     | `p-startup-scale` | $300-1500 |
  | Production at Scale | `p-enterprise`    | $2k+      |

  - Each `profiles/<id>/` directory MUST contain: `README.md`, `META.yaml`
    (kind: Profile), `terraform.tfvars`, `ansible/group_vars.yml`,
    `crossplane/composition-pins.yaml`, `helm-values/`, `secretspec.toml`,
    `argocd/appset-overrides.yaml`, `nx/preset.json`.
  - Custom profiles via `task profile:fork <base> <new-id>`. CI matrix gates
    only the 5 named profiles; forks are user-owned.
  - Profile dimensions are the 12 axes from spec Section 1.6. Every named
    profile picks a coherent set across all 12.
  ```

  ```markdown
  <!-- docs/architecture/seven-layers.md -->

  # The seven layers (engineer reference)

  Authoritative source: spec Section 1.2. This page is the engineer-facing
  expansion. Founder-facing version: `apps/marketing/app/architecture/page.tsx`.

  ## Layer 0a — Launcher CLI + marketing site

  Founder entrypoint. `npx create-platform@latest` (or `task init` after
  clone) runs the 7-stage wizard (spec Section 11.3): project identity →
  profile recommender → cloud → secret backend → domain + TLS → reference
  apps → materialize. Emits ADRs to `docs/adrs/` and appends to
  `.audit/decisions.jsonl` per stage. Code at `internal/cli/`.

  ## Layer 0b — MCP server

  Agent entrypoint. Ships as `@ts-monorepo-template/mcp-server` (npm) and
  `internal/mcp-server/`. Tool catalog (spec Section 1.8): `list_profiles`,
  `describe_profile`, `recommend_profile`, `list_apps`, `describe_app`,
  `add_app`, `list_xrds`, `describe_xrd`, `claim_infra`, `simulate_cost`,
  `explain_tradeoff`, `validate_plan`, `propose_change`.

  ## Layer 1 — Verb surface

  Engineers and agents type only `task <verb>`. Taskfile delegates to the
  layer underneath. Full verb list in `Taskfile.yml`; founder-safe subset
  enumerated in `AGENTS.md`.

  ## Layer 2 — Toolchain + secrets

  `devenv.nix` pins every language toolchain (spec Section 4.2). `direnv`
  auto-activates the shell. Secrets via `secretspec.toml` only; OS keyring
  is the local cache, Azure Key Vault is the team source of truth (per
  profile selection).

  ## Layer 3 — Build orchestration

  Nx 21 with inferred plugins for Go (`@nx-go/nx-go`), Python (`@nxlv/python`),
  Rust (`@monodon/rust`), TypeScript (`@nx/js`). Nx Cloud token lives only in
  GH Actions secrets; local builds run unauthenticated.

  ## Layer 4 — Container build

  BuildKit per-language multi-stage Dockerfiles under
  `internal/templates/dockerfiles/`. cosign keyless OIDC signing via the
  GitHub Actions identity. SBOMs per image.

  ## Layer 5 — App runtime

  `infra/helm/lib-chart/` is the only Helm artifact apps depend on.
  SecurityContext FLOOR + NetworkPolicy default-deny + observability wiring
  (OTel, ServiceMonitor, PodMonitor) are baked in.

  ## Layer 6 — Platform infra

  Crossplane providers + functions + XRDs + Compositions. Four XRD bundles
  ship Day-1: core service primitives, observability + identity, schema
  governance + Kroxylicious, cloud bootstrap. ESO bridges
  Crossplane-published Secrets into app namespaces.

  ## Layer 7 — Bootstrap

  Optional. `infra/terraform/modules/<provider>/` for the 7 supported clouds
  (Contabo, Hetzner Cloud, OVH, Azure, AWS, GCP, Cloudflare).
  Kubespray-style configurable Ansible playbooks under `infra/ansible/`.
  ```

  ```markdown
  <!-- docs/architecture/profiles.md -->

  # Profiles — engineer reference

  Authoritative source: spec Sections 1.5 + 1.6. Profile catalog in
  `profiles/`. Each profile is a coherent pick across the 12 axes from
  spec Section 1.6.

  | Founder label       | Machine ID        | $/mo band | Cluster substrate        |
  | ------------------- | ----------------- | --------- | ------------------------ |
  | Just Me             | `p-solo`          | $0        | local-k3d                |
  | Side Project        | `p-hobby`         | $5-20     | single-VPS k3s           |
  | Early Startup       | `p-startup-small` | $30-150   | bare-VM k3s 3-node       |
  | Scaling Startup     | `p-startup-scale` | $300-1500 | managed-K8s multi-AZ     |
  | Production at Scale | `p-enterprise`    | $2k+      | managed-K8s multi-region |

  ## The 12 axes

  team_size, env_count, target_budget_usd, compliance_floor, workload_shape,
  ha_level, cluster_substrate, mesh, observability_depth, secret_backend,
  registry, cdn_edge. Full ranges in spec Section 1.6.

  ## Per-profile bringup

  See `docs/dev/bringup-p-solo.md` ... `docs/dev/bringup-p-enterprise.md`.

  ## Forking a profile

  `task profile:fork <base-id> <new-id>` copies `profiles/<base-id>/` to
  `profiles/<new-id>/`, rewrites `META.yaml` metadata.name, and adds the
  new profile to `profiles/index.yaml`. CI matrix gates only the 5 named
  profiles; forks are user-owned.
  ```

  ```markdown
  <!-- docs/architecture/decision-model.md -->

  # Decision model — ADRs, audit log, recommender

  Every architectural fork emits three artifacts (spec Sections 11.6, 15.9,
  15.10): an ADR under `docs/adrs/NNNN-<topic>.md`, a JSONL line in
  `.audit/decisions.jsonl`, and (for profile selection) a recommender output
  with `rubric_sha256` so a future audit can prove which rubric version
  produced the recommendation.

  ## ADR lifecycle

  - Statuses: `proposed`, `accepted`, `superseded`, `deprecated`.
  - Template at `docs/adrs/_template.md`.
  - `task adr:new <topic>` scaffolds the next-numbered ADR.
  - `task adr:index` regenerates `docs/adrs/README.md`.
  - Launcher auto-emits ADRs for each wizard stage (12+ on a default
    `p-hobby` run, per spec Section 15.9 Day-1 inventory).

  ## Audit log integrity

  `.audit/decisions.jsonl` is append-only and SHA-256-chained.
  `sha256_self = sha256(sha256_prev || canonical_json(line_without_sha256_self))`.
  Genesis line has `sha256_prev = "0".repeat(64)`. Verbs (spec Section 15.10):

  - `task audit:append` — internal; called by launcher / MCP / CI under flock.
  - `task audit:verify` — walks the chain; exits 1 on first break with line.
  - `task audit:export` — renders to `docs/audit/timeline.md`.
  - `task audit:diff` — compares two snapshots.

  Verify implementation lives at `internal/cli/audit-verify/` (Go, ~80 LOC).

  ## Profile recommender

  Deterministic rubric at `internal/cli/src/recommender/rubric.yaml`. Pure
  function `score(answers, rubric) -> ranked[]`. Output captures
  `rubric_version` and `rubric_sha256`. The MCP tool `recommend_profile`
  wraps the same function (spec Section 11.4).
  ```

  ````markdown
  <!-- docs/agents/aegis.md -->

  # Aegis (reference MCP consumer)

  Aegis is the reference consumer of the platform MCP server (spec Section
  1.8 + 11.11). Any Claude / Codex / Cursor agent that speaks the Model
  Context Protocol can drive the same tool surface — Aegis is just the
  one we use to validate the contract in CI (spec Section 14.7).

  ## What Aegis does

  - Reads the `META.yaml` cascade from any directory.
  - Calls MCP tools to introspect profiles, apps, XRDs.
  - Proposes changes via `propose_change` (returns structured patch +
    ADR draft + audit log entry; never writes the working tree directly).
  - Validates plans via `validate_plan` (dry-run-validates across all 7
    layers before any patch is applied).

  ## How to point Aegis at the in-repo server

  ```bash
  task mcp:serve  # launches internal/mcp-server/ on a local socket
  aegis --mcp-endpoint=unix:///tmp/platform-mcp.sock
  ```
  ````

  ## How CI validates the contract

  `.github/workflows/pr.yml` job `mcp-validate` runs the Aegis test harness
  against `internal/mcp-server/` for every PR (see spec Section 14.7).
  Schema regressions fail the build.

  ````
  ```markdown
  <!-- docs/agents/mcp-tool-reference.md -->
  # MCP tool reference

  Authoritative source: spec Section 1.8 + 11.8. Schemas under
  `internal/mcp-server/tools/*.schema.json`. Every tool below is exposed
  by both the npm package `@ts-monorepo-template/mcp-server` and the
  in-repo `internal/mcp-server/`.

  ## Profile tools

  - `list_profiles` — enumerate the 5 named profiles with tradeoff summary.
  - `describe_profile` — full per-profile tradeoff structure (12 axes).
  - `recommend_profile` — 10 questions in, ranked profile + reasoning out.
    Records `rubric_sha256` in the response.

  ## App tools

  - `list_apps` — inventory current monorepo apps with capability descriptors.
  - `describe_app` — META.yaml + lib-chart values + claims for one app.
  - `add_app` — scaffold a new polyglot app under a profile's constraints.

  ## Infra tools

  - `list_xrds` — enumerate Crossplane platform XRDs.
  - `describe_xrd` — schema, capabilities, cost band, composition options.
  - `claim_infra` — scaffold an XR claim (e.g. `XPostgresCluster` for
    `app-foo`) under the right env.

  ## Decision tools

  - `simulate_cost` — current state + projected traffic → estimated $/mo
    per layer.
  - `explain_tradeoff` — diff (files + resources + cost) of switching
    from one profile to another.
  - `validate_plan` — dry-run-validates any proposed change across the
    seven layers (helm template + crossplane render + tf plan + ansible
    syntax-check).
  - `propose_change` — produces a structured patch + ADR draft + audit
    log entry. Does not write the working tree.

  ## Day-1 implementation status (spec Section 1.10)

  Implemented Day-1: `list_profiles`, `describe_profile`, `recommend_profile`,
  `list_apps`, `simulate_cost`, `explain_tradeoff`. The remaining tools
  ship as scaffolded stubs with stable schemas; bodies land in follow-up PRs.
  ````

  ````markdown
  <!-- docs/agents/agents-md-cascade.md -->

  # AGENTS.md cascade — resolution rules

  Authoritative source: spec Section 15.8. Reference: https://agents.md/.

  ## The 6 levels

  | Level    | File                   | Scope                                          |
  | -------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
  | Root     | `AGENTS.md`            | Founder-safe verbs, project rules, never-do    |
  | Apps     | `apps/AGENTS.md`       | App-build conventions                          |
  | Per-app  | `apps/<svc>/AGENTS.md` | Architecture invariants, common tasks          |
  | Packages | `packages/AGENTS.md`   | Library conventions                            |
  | Internal | `internal/AGENTS.md`   | Schemas, error catalog, glossary editing rules |
  | Infra    | `infra/AGENTS.md`      | Helm/Crossplane/Terraform conventions          |
  | Profiles | `profiles/AGENTS.md`   | Profile authoring rules                        |

  ## Resolution rule

  Agents reading directory `D` MUST resolve `AGENTS.md` by walking
  `D -> parent -> ... -> repo root` and merging shallow, child-wins.
  Same rule as `META.yaml`.

  ## Pseudocode

  ```text
  function resolveAgentsMd(dir):
    chain = []
    while dir != repoRoot.parent:
      if exists(dir + "/AGENTS.md"):
        chain.unshift(read(dir + "/AGENTS.md"))
      dir = parent(dir)
    return shallowMerge(chain)  // last (= deepest) wins per top-level key
  ```
  ````

  ## What "child-wins" means in markdown

  Sections with identical `## ` headings: the deeper file's section
  replaces the shallower one wholesale. Sections present only in the
  shallower file are inherited unchanged.

  ```

  ```

  ````markdown
  # Bringup — `p-solo` (Just Me, $0)

  Local k3d, no cloud. For weekend hacking.

  ## 3-command bringup

  ```bash
  npx create-platform@latest --profile p-solo
  cd <slug>
  task launch
  task open
  ```
  ````

  ## What `task launch` does on `p-solo`
  - Boots a local k3d cluster (1 server, 0 agents).
  - Installs `lib-chart` deps + Crossplane core (no providers).
  - Renders the 3 reference apps (go-hello, py-hello, rs-hello) into the
    local registry via `k3d image import`.
  - Skips Argo CD; reconciliation is via `task sync:local`.

  ## What you do NOT get on `p-solo`
  - No HA, no observability stack (metrics-only), no cloud secrets — uses
    OS keyring only.

  ````
  ```markdown
  <!-- docs/dev/bringup-p-hobby.md -->
  # Bringup — `p-hobby` (Side Project, $5-20/mo)

  Single VPS (Contabo default), k3s, Longhorn-less.

  ## 3-command bringup

  ```bash
  npx create-platform@latest --profile p-hobby
  cd <slug>
  task launch
  task open
  ````

  ## What `task launch` does on `p-hobby`
  - Provisions one VPS via `infra/terraform/modules/contabo/`.
  - Runs the Kubespray-style Ansible playbook → k3s single-node.
  - Installs Crossplane + ESO + Argo CD + lib-chart.
  - Argo CD root app reconciles the 3 reference apps + cnpg-single XRD claim.
  - Caddy ingress with Cloudflare DNS-01 TLS (if a domain was selected at
    `npx create-platform` time).

  ## Cost guardrails

  Composition pin `cnpg-single` (not `cnpg-ha`). Redis without Sentinel.
  MinIO single-node. Cost simulator (`task simulate-cost`) confirms the
  $5-20/mo band before `task launch` proceeds.

  ````
  ```markdown
  <!-- docs/dev/bringup-p-startup-small.md -->
  # Bringup — `p-startup-small` (Early Startup, $30-150/mo)

  3 VPS (Hetzner Cloud default), k3s HA, Longhorn.

  ## 3-command bringup

  ```bash
  npx create-platform@latest --profile p-startup-small
  cd <slug>
  task launch
  task open
  ````

  ## What `task launch` does on `p-startup-small`
  - Provisions 3 VPS via `infra/terraform/modules/hetzner/`.
  - Ansible bootstraps k3s in HA mode (embedded etcd, 3 control planes).
  - Longhorn for stateful (cnpg-ha, redis-sentinel, minio-distributed).
  - Vault on-cluster for secret backend (per profile META.yaml).
  - Argo CD with 2 envs (dev + prod) via ApplicationSet matrix.

  ````
  ```markdown
  <!-- docs/dev/bringup-p-startup-scale.md -->
  # Bringup — `p-startup-scale` (Scaling Startup, $300-1500/mo)

  Managed K8s (AKS or EKS or GKE), multi-AZ, managed databases.

  ## 3-command bringup

  ```bash
  npx create-platform@latest --profile p-startup-scale
  cd <slug>
  task launch
  task open
  ````

  ## What `task launch` does on `p-startup-scale`
  - Provisions the chosen managed K8s via the cloud's Terraform module.
  - Compositions swap to `rds-managed` for XPostgres, managed Redis for
    XCache, native blob for XBlob.
  - Argo CD with 3 envs (dev + staging + prod). Kargo promotion enabled.
  - Linkerd service mesh enabled by default (`mesh: linkerd` in profile).

  ````
  ```markdown
  <!-- docs/dev/bringup-p-enterprise.md -->
  # Bringup — `p-enterprise` (Production at Scale, $2k+/mo)

  Multi-region managed K8s, compliance-floor SOC2-ready, full audit trail.

  ## 3-command bringup

  ```bash
  npx create-platform@latest --profile p-enterprise
  cd <slug>
  task launch
  task open
  ````

  ## What `task launch` does on `p-enterprise`
  - Provisions 2 regions of managed K8s. Cross-region Crossplane providers.
  - Compositions: `rds-multi-az` for XPostgres, native multi-region Redis.
  - Vault HA + ESO with AKV-or-equivalent primary.
  - Argo CD with N envs (per-tenant matrix). Kargo + sync windows.
  - cosign signature enforcement at admission (policy controller).

  ## Day-1 caveat (spec Section 1.10)

  Full nightly CI bringup of `p-enterprise` is gated manual (cost cap).
  The template renders + plans cleanly; an operator runs `task launch`
  with eyes on the bill.

  ```typescript
  // apps/marketing/app/lib/profile-loader.ts
  import { readFile, readdir } from 'node:fs/promises'
  import { resolve } from 'node:path'
  import { parse as parseYaml } from 'yaml'

  const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', '..')

  export type Profile = {
    machineId: string
    founderLabel: string
    costBandUsdMo: [number, number]
    tagline: string
  }

  const TAGLINES: Record<string, string> = {
    'p-solo': "I'm hacking on something this weekend.",
    'p-hobby': 'Maybe 100 users, single VPS, $5-20/mo.',
    'p-startup-small': '2-10 of us, real customers, basic HA.',
    'p-startup-scale': 'Funded, multi-env, multi-AZ, real SLA.',
    'p-enterprise': 'Multi-region, compliance, audit trail.',
  }

  export async function loadProfiles(): Promise<Profile[]> {
    const dir = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'profiles')
    const entries = await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })
    const out: Profile[] = []
    for (const entry of entries) {
      if (!entry.isDirectory() || !entry.name.startsWith('p-')) continue
      const metaPath = resolve(dir, entry.name, 'META.yaml')
      const raw = parseYaml(await readFile(metaPath, 'utf8')) as {
        metadata: { founderLabel: string }
        spec: { costBandUsdMo: [number, number] }
      }
      out.push({
        machineId: entry.name,
        founderLabel: raw.metadata.founderLabel,
        costBandUsdMo: raw.spec.costBandUsdMo,
        tagline: TAGLINES[entry.name] ?? '',
      })
    }
    const order = ['p-solo', 'p-hobby', 'p-startup-small', 'p-startup-scale', 'p-enterprise']
    return out.sort((a, b) => order.indexOf(a.machineId) - order.indexOf(b.machineId))
  }
  ```

  ```typescript
              <dd>

              </dd>
            </div>
          ))}
        </dl>
      </main>
    )
  }
  ```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the generator + Astro config + Taskfile verbs + CI workflow**

  ```typescript
  // apps/docs-public/scripts/generate-references.ts
  import { mkdir, readFile, readdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
  import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
  import { resolve, basename } from 'node:path'
  import { parse as parseYaml } from 'yaml'

  const ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..')
  const OUT = resolve(ROOT, 'apps/docs-public/src/content/docs/reference')

  const LAYERS = [
    ['00a-launcher', 'Layer 0a — Launcher CLI'],
    ['00b-mcp', 'Layer 0b — MCP server'],
    ['01-verbs', 'Layer 1 — Verb surface'],
    ['02-toolchain', 'Layer 2 — Toolchain + secrets'],
    ['03-build', 'Layer 3 — Build orchestration'],
    ['04-container', 'Layer 4 — Container build'],
    ['05-runtime', 'Layer 5 — App runtime'],
    ['06-platform', 'Layer 6 — Platform infra'],
    ['07-bootstrap', 'Layer 7 — Bootstrap'],
  ] as const

  async function genLayers() {
    await mkdir(resolve(OUT, 'layers'), { recursive: true })
    for (const [slug, title] of LAYERS) {
      const body = `---\ntitle: ${title}\n---\n\nSee \`docs/architecture/seven-layers.md\` for the engineer reference.\n`
      await writeFile(resolve(OUT, 'layers', `${slug}.md`), body)
    }
  }

  async function genFromMetaDir(srcDir: string, outSub: string) {
    const src = resolve(ROOT, srcDir)
    if (!existsSync(src)) return
    await mkdir(resolve(OUT, outSub), { recursive: true })
    for (const entry of await readdir(src, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (!entry.isDirectory()) continue
      const metaPath = resolve(src, entry.name, 'META.yaml')
      if (!existsSync(metaPath)) continue
      const meta = parseYaml(await readFile(metaPath, 'utf8')) as {
        metadata: { name: string }
        spec?: unknown
      }
      const body = `---\ntitle: ${meta.metadata.name}\n---\n\n\`\`\`yaml\n${await readFile(metaPath, 'utf8')}\n\`\`\`\n`
      await writeFile(resolve(OUT, outSub, `${entry.name}.md`), body)
    }
  }

  async function genVerbs() {
    await mkdir(resolve(OUT, 'verbs'), { recursive: true })
    const taskfile = await readFile(resolve(ROOT, 'Taskfile.yml'), 'utf8')
    const re = /^\s*([a-z][a-z0-9:-]*):\s*$/gm
    const seen = new Set<string>()
    let m: RegExpExecArray | null
    while ((m = re.exec(taskfile))) {
      const verb = m[1]
      if (verb === 'version' || verb === 'tasks' || verb === 'includes') continue
      if (seen.has(verb)) continue
      seen.add(verb)
      const body = `---\ntitle: task ${verb}\n---\n\nSee \`Taskfile.yml\` for the executable definition.\n`
      await writeFile(resolve(OUT, 'verbs', `${verb.replace(/:/g, '-')}.md`), body)
    }
  }

  async function main() {
    await mkdir(OUT, { recursive: true })
    await genLayers()
    await genFromMetaDir('infra/crossplane/xrds', 'xrds')
    await genFromMetaDir('infra/helm/apps', 'apps')
    await genFromMetaDir('profiles', 'profiles')
    await genVerbs()
    console.log('docs:gen wrote reference pages to', OUT)
  }

  main().catch((e) => {
    console.error(e)
    process.exit(1)
  })
  ```

  ```mdx
  ---
  title: ts-monorepo-template documentation
  ---

  # Engineer documentation

  Reference docs only. How-tos live on the marketing site
  (`apps/marketing/`).

  - **Layers** — one page per architectural layer (0a, 0b, 1-7).
  - **Verbs** — one page per `Taskfile.yml` target.
  - **XRDs** — one page per Crossplane XRD bundle (generated from META.yaml).
  - **Apps** — one page per app chart under `infra/helm/apps/`.
  - **Profiles** — one page per named profile.

  Drift between code and docs fails the CI build (`task docs:gen` is
  re-run in CI; a non-empty diff against the committed tree is a hard
  fail, per spec Section 15.4).
  ```

  ```yaml
  # Taskfile.yml (append under `tasks:`)
  docs:gen:
    desc: Regenerate apps/docs-public/ reference pages from code
    cmds:
      - pnpm tsx apps/docs-public/scripts/generate-references.ts

  docs:quickstart-verify:
    desc: CI gate — assert the documented 3-command Quickstart matches launcher output
    cmds:
      - npx --yes create-platform@latest --profile p-hobby --dry-run > /tmp/launcher-out.txt
      - grep -F 'task launch' /tmp/launcher-out.txt
      - grep -F 'task open' /tmp/launcher-out.txt
      - grep -F 'npx create-platform@latest' apps/marketing/app/quickstart/page.tsx
  ```

  ```yaml
  # .github/workflows/site-build.yml
  name: site-build
  on:
    pull_request:
      paths:
        - apps/marketing/**
        - apps/docs-public/**
        - docs/**
        - Taskfile.yml
        - .github/workflows/site-build.yml
  jobs:
    astro:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
          with: { version: 9 }
        - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
          with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'pnpm' }
        - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        - name: Regenerate docs and assert no drift
          run: |
            task docs:gen
            git diff --exit-code apps/docs-public/src/content/docs/reference
        - name: astro check
          run: pnpm --filter docs-public exec astro check
        - name: astro build
          run: pnpm --filter docs-public exec astro build
        - name: broken-link check
          run: pnpm dlx linkinator apps/docs-public/dist --skip 'localhost|127.0.0.1' --recurse
        - name: lighthouse-ci budget
          run: pnpm dlx @lhci/cli@0.13.x autorun --collect.staticDistDir=apps/docs-public/dist --assert.preset=lighthouse:recommended
    quickstart-verify:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
          with: { version: 9 }
        - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
          with: { node-version: '20', cache: 'pnpm' }
        - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        - name: Verify documented Quickstart matches launcher output
          run: task docs:quickstart-verify
  ```

  ```yaml
    engineer: 'profiles/<id>/META.yaml missing or invalid; ajv validation failed.'
    link: /troubleshoot/profile-not-found
  - code: PROFILE_COST_OVER_BUDGET
    founder: 'The cost simulator says this profile costs more than your target budget. Switch profile or raise budget.'
    engineer: 'simulate_cost result exceeds spec.costBandUsdMo upper bound; refused by launcher guardrail.'
    link: /troubleshoot/profile-cost-over-budget
  - code: CLUSTER_NOT_REACHABLE
    founder: "We couldn't reach your cluster. Check your VPN, `kubectl cluster-info`, and that the cluster is running."
    engineer: 'kubectl API request returned a connection error; check KUBECONFIG and current-context.'
    link: /troubleshoot/cluster-not-reachable
  - code: CROSSPLANE_PROVIDER_NOT_HEALTHY
    founder: 'A platform provider is unhealthy. Run `task xp:doctor` to see which one and why.'
    engineer: 'Provider .status.conditions has Healthy=False; common causes: image pull, RBAC, leader election.'
    link: /troubleshoot/crossplane-provider-not-healthy
  - code: ARGOCD_APP_OUT_OF_SYNC
    founder: 'Argo CD says an app is out of sync. Run `task argo:sync <app>` or check the diff in the UI.'
    engineer: 'Application status.sync.status = OutOfSync; inspect status.conditions for the cause.'
    link: /troubleshoot/argocd-app-out-of-sync
  - code: HELM_LINT_FAILED
    founder: "A chart isn't valid. The launcher refused to deploy it. Open the linked page for details."
    engineer: 'helm lint produced errors; usually missing required values or invalid YAML in overlays.'
    link: /troubleshoot/helm-lint-failed
  - code: COSIGN_VERIFY_FAILED
    founder: "An image signature didn't verify. The cluster will refuse to run this image until you re-sign it."
    engineer: 'cosign verify failed; check Fulcio cert chain, OIDC issuer, and identity expressions.'
    link: /troubleshoot/cosign-verify-failed
  - code: TERRAFORM_PLAN_DRIFT
    founder: "Your cloud state drifted from what's in git. Run `task tf:plan` to see what changed."
    engineer: 'terraform plan returned non-empty diff; investigate before apply.'
    link: /troubleshoot/terraform-plan-drift
  - code: ANSIBLE_HOST_UNREACHABLE
    founder: "Ansible couldn't SSH to a node. Check that the node is up and your SSH key is loaded."
    engineer: 'ansible host returned UNREACHABLE; verify inventory + ansible_host + ssh-agent.'
    link: /troubleshoot/ansible-host-unreachable
  - code: NX_CLOUD_TOKEN_MISSING
    founder: "Nx Cloud isn't authenticated. CI builds will work; local builds run uncached. No action required."
    engineer: 'NX_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN not set; expected only in GH Actions (spec Section 3.1).'
    link: /troubleshoot/nx-cloud-token-missing
  - code: MCP_TOOL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
    founder: "That agent action isn't available on Day-1. See the linked page for the deferred-tool roadmap."
    engineer: 'MCP tool returned status=DEFERRED per spec Section 1.10.'
    link: /troubleshoot/mcp-tool-not-implemented
  - code: AUDIT_LOG_CHAIN_BROKEN
    founder: 'Your decision history file looks tampered. Run `task audit:verify` for the exact line.'
    engineer: 'sha256_self mismatch at line N; spec Section 15.10 chain rule violated.'
    link: /troubleshoot/audit-log-chain-broken
  - code: ADR_MISSING_FOR_DECISION
    founder: 'A decision was made but no ADR was written. Run `task adr:new` to backfill.'
    engineer: 'audit log line has no adr_emitted; expected for every architectural-fork stage.'
    link: /troubleshoot/adr-missing-for-decision
  ```
